For 'two massive bodies', particle-level and body-level gating differ. The record's gate is a property of each chi quantum (mu = the quantum's own fiber width, #6 sec. 4). In a long-range model (b), the force between two extended bodies is the gate averaged over constituent pairs. For a Gaussian gate and Maxwellian bodies, <W> = (1 + 2s^2/v*^2)^(-3/2) exp(-V^2/(v*^2 + 2s^2)), with s^2 = s1^2 + s2^2 and V the bulk relative velocity (checked against quadrature). Bound ordinary matter would see a nearly shut gate (electrons ~2000 km/s give about 3e-4), and a composition-dependent one. So P13 and P20's bulk-velocity gating of ordinary bodies is not what a constituent-level gate gives; equivalence-principle tests would set that bound instead. Script: v7_body_gate_and_jeans.py.
